pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/jobseeker/adapters/registry.ts:61 Three modules that do not reference each other each restate which config key a vendor reads and how its host is derived: the adapter (greenhouse.ts:36 reads cfg(ctx.source, "token")), registry.hostForAdapter, and the discover probe list. Renaming or adding a vendor's config key means three edits, and only the registry's switch is compiler-checked.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/jobseeker/adapters/registry.ts:61 Information leakage: the per-vendor config key and host rule are re-encoded outside the adapter because SourceAdapter has no host(config) member. That puts the same decision in two places (here and greenhouse.ts:36).

app/_lib/jobseeker/adapters/ats/discover.ts:25 The probe list restates the config key { token } a third time, plus a per-vendor shape regex. Changing one vendor touches the adapter, the registry and discover, which is scattered change. Judged from structure; the history is one commit, so no scatter was measured.

app/_lib/jobseeker/adapters/types.ts:2 The adapter seam takes the fetcher from AdapterContext, so the real politeFetch and the scripted test fetch are two adapters of one PoliteFetch type. adapters.test.ts runs a shared KP_OFFLINE contract over every adapter in the registry.

app/_lib/jobseeker/adapters/ats/greenhouse.ts:42 The loop skips, mutates raw.company, yields and stops at a cap. Effects are mixed into the classification, so explicit sequential code is the right form.

app/_lib/jobseeker/adapters/ats/greenhouse.ts:12 The vendor mapping is already a pure function, and the adapter tests need only one double (the scripted fetch). None of the technique's triggers (two or more doubles, several runtimes) holds.
app/_lib/jobseeker/adapters/adapters.test.ts:26 Every input (source row, JSON body) is a plain value a test can construct, so there is no host-only type to mirror.

pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: app/features/library/jobs/jobsCoachPoolCap.test.ts:16 There is no seam where the route's poolTruncated decision or the panel's admission can be exercised, so the test regex-matches source text (e.g. /const \{ entries, truncated \}/). That pins how the code is written rather than what it does, and a behaviour-preserving refactor turns it red.

techniques.evidence: app/features/library/jobs/jobsCoachPoolCap.test.ts:16 This is the technique's named failure for seamless code: a test that reaches into the implementation (source text) because no seam lets the behaviour be reached.

app/features/library/jobs/jobsAgentFitLogic.ts:2 useAgentFitLogic has a single caller (JobsAgentFitTab) and returns a 24-member bag, including `t`, which the caller also builds itself. The stated reason for the split is a line cap, which the technique calls a metric, not a reason. Counterexample in the same context: jobsCoachApply.ts:8-10 keeps one deep-link grammar for both ends.
app/features/library/jobs/jobsAgentFitModel.ts:1 The verdict, coverage, spec-form and timeline logic is pure and tested under node:test. The hook is the only driver that does I/O.

techniques.evidence: app/features/library/jobs/jobsRediscoveryFeedLogic.ts:237 Depth in the wrong place: the caller works around the module's interface instead of using it, and the 'added' decision is encoded in two modules. app/features/library/jobs/jobsRediscoveryFeedLogic.ts:11 The feed and JobsRediscoverPanel (useAddToPipeline) both reach pipeline-add through one shared module rather than calling the route directly.

pairs.evidence: app/features/tools/analyze/history/HistoryTypes.ts:14 The client hand-restates the analysis list row (AnalysisRow) instead of deriving it from the server's AnalysisListRow in app/_lib/db/analyses.ts.
